Combien de notes différentes compte une: How many different notes does a pentatonic scale have?
Penta veut dire cinq. Les cinq touches n: Penta means five. The five black keys of the piano form one.
Combien de préludes et fugues compte cha: How many preludes and fugues does each book of Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier contain?
Un prélude et une fugue dans chacune des: One prelude and one fugue in each of the 12 major and 12 minor keys: 24 pairs per book.
Dans une gamme majeure, les demi-tons to: In a major scale, the half steps fall between the 3rd and 4th notes, and between the 7th and 8th.

C, G, D, A: three fifths.

Joseph Fourier, dans sa Théorie analytiq: Joseph Fourier, in his Analytical Theory of Heat, in 1822. The tool is now used to analyze every sound.

C'est le cas de la clarinette dans son r: This is the case of the clarinet in its low register, which gives it its somewhat hollow timbre.

Il décompose le son en ses fréquences, à: It breaks the sound down into its frequencies, the way Fourier did: you see the fundamental and its harmonics.

Mêmes notes, autre note à la basse. Rame: Same notes, a different note in the bass. Rameau theorized it in 1722.

5/4 pour la tierce majeure, 6/5 pour la: 5/4 for the major third, 6/5 for the minor third.
En do majeur, quelle cadence parfaite co: In C major, which perfect cadence ends a piece?

Selon la théorie classique, plus le rapp: According to classical theory, the simpler the frequency ratio between two notes, the more consonant they sound.
Helmholtz l'expliquait par les battement: Helmholtz explained it by beats: with a simple ratio, few neighboring harmonics rub against each other.
Qui publie en 1722 le Traité de l'harmon: Who published in 1722 the Treatise on Harmony Reduced to Its Natural Principles?
Rameau, organiste et compositeur, y pose: Rameau, an organist and composer, sets out the theory of inversions and the fundamental bass.
Un do vibre à 264 Hz. Avec le rapport 5/: A C vibrates at 264 Hz. With the 5/4 ratio, at how many hertz does its natural major third sound?
f = 264 × 5/4 = 330 Hz. Zarlino défendit: f = 264 × 5/4 = 330 Hz. Zarlino championed these pure 5/4 thirds in 1558, against the Pythagorean third of 81/64.
L'écart entre douze quintes pures et sep: The gap between twelve pure fifths and seven octaves
Douze quintes de 3/2 dépassent sept octa: Twelve fifths of 3/2 overshoot seven octaves by about 1.4%: you never land exactly back on your feet.
Combien de cents dans une octave ?: How many cents in an octave?
Alexander Ellis a inventé le cent dans l: Alexander Ellis invented the cent in the 1880s: one hundredth of a tempered semitone. 12 × 100 = 1,200.
Dans le tempérament égal, tous les demi-: In equal temperament, all semitones have the same frequency ratio.
C'est sa définition : douze demi-tons de: That is its definition: twelve semitones with a ratio of ¹²√2.

(3/2)¹² is about 129.75 and 2⁷ = 128. What gap, as a percentage rounded to the tenth, separates twelve fifths from seven octaves?

Une quinte du tempérament égal est un pe: A fifth in equal temperament is slightly smaller than a pure fifth.
Environ 1,4983 au lieu de 1,5, soit 2 ce: About 1.4983 instead of 1.5, that is, 2 cents less: the ear barely notices.
Qui a calculé le premier, en 1584, une d: Who first calculated, in 1584, an exact division of the octave into twelve equal semitones?
Zhu Zaiyu calcule au boulier la racine d: Zhu Zaiyu computed the twelfth root of 2 on an abacus, to 24 exact decimals. In Europe, Simon Stevin worked on the same idea at the same time.
Combien de cents dans un demi-ton tempér: How many cents in a tempered semitone?
C'est la définition du cent : le centièm: That is the definition of the cent: one hundredth of a tempered semitone.
Le titre du Clavier bien tempéré prouve: The title of the Well-Tempered Clavier proves that Bach tuned in equal temperament.
« Bien tempéré » veut dire assez bien ac: “Well-tempered” means tuned well enough for every key. The exact tuning Bach used is still debated.
Pourquoi accorde-t-on presque tous les p: Why are almost all pianos tuned in equal temperament?
Pour jouer dans toutes les tonalités san: To play in every key without a glaring wrong note
Parce que les quintes y sont pures: Because the fifths are pure in it
Pour que l'octave sonne plus large: To make the octave sound wider
Chaque intervalle est un peu faux, mais: Each interval is slightly off, but all equally so: you can change key freely.

Au-dessous de 20 Hz, ce sont des infraso: Below 20 Hz is infrasound; above 20,000 Hz, ultrasound, which bats can hear.

L = 10 log₁₀(I / I₀) : +10 dB multiplie: L = 10 log₁₀(I / I₀): +10 dB multiplies the intensity by 10, so +20 dB multiplies it by 10 × 10 = 100. The bel is named after Alexander Graham Bell; the decibel is a tenth of it.
Avec l'âge, on perd d'abord l'audition d: With age, you first lose the hearing of low sounds.
On perd d'abord les aigus : c'est la pre: You lose the high frequencies first: this is presbycusis.
Qu'ont mesuré Harvey Fletcher et Wilden: What did Harvey Fletcher and Wilden Munson measure in 1933?
La sensibilité de l'oreille selon la fré: The ear's sensitivity depending on frequency
La vitesse du son dans l'eau: The speed of sound in water

Leurs courbes montrent qu'un son grave d: Their curves show that a low sound must be much more intense than a 3,000 Hz sound to seem as loud.
L'effet Mozart, qui rendrait durablement: The Mozart effect, supposed to make you lastingly smarter, has been confirmed.
L'étude de 1993 décrivait un gain bref s: The 1993 study described a brief gain on a spatial task. In 1999, a meta-analysis concluded the effect was small, with no change in IQ.

Valorie Salimpoor et ses collègues l'ont: Valorie Salimpoor and her colleagues measured it with brain imaging: the same molecule as for food.

10^(3/10) ≈ 2 : trois décibels de plus,: 10^(3/10) ≈ 2: three more decibels is roughly twice the intensity.
Vers quelles fréquences l'oreille est-el: Around which frequencies is the ear most sensitive?
C'est la zone où passe une bonne part de: It is the zone that carries much of speech intelligibility, and where the outer ear resonates.
Beethoven a composé sa Neuvième Symphoni: Beethoven composed his Ninth Symphony when he was almost completely deaf.
À la création, en 1824 à Vienne, il étai: At the premiere, in Vienna in 1824, he was on stage next to the actual conductor; the singer Caroline Unger had to turn him toward the audience so he could see the applause.
Nommer une note entendue sans note de ré: Naming a note heard without a reference note
Une capacité rare : la plupart des music: A rare ability: most musicians have relative pitch, which recognizes intervals.
Le hertz est adopté par la Commission él: The hertz was adopted by the International Electrotechnical Commission in 1930, then by the General Conference on Weights and Measures in 1960. Hertz had died in 1894, aged 36.
Dès 1630, Marin Mersenne mesure la vites: As early as 1630, Marin Mersenne measured the speed of sound by timing the gap between the flash of a gunshot and its bang. He found about 448 m/s, too high.
En 1738, l'Académie des sciences de Pari: In 1738, the Paris Academy of Sciences fired cannon on a windless day and found about 332 m/s at 0 °C, within 1% of the modern value. In 1740, Bianconi showed that sound travels faster in warm air.
En 1636, dans son Harmonie universelle,: In 1636, in his Harmonie universelle, Marin Mersenne set out the laws of strings: frequency falls as the string gets longer and rises as it is tightened.
Newton trouvait dans les Principia (1687: In the Principia (1687), Newton found about 298 m/s, too low. Laplace explained the error in the early 19th century: air compressed by the wave has no time to exchange its heat.
En 1841, sur le lac Léman, Jean-Daniel C: In 1841, on Lake Geneva, Jean-Daniel Colladon showed that sound travels over four times faster in water than in air. With Charles Sturm, he had received an Académie des sciences prize for this measurement.
John Shore, trompettiste et luthiste de: John Shore, a trumpeter and lutenist at the English court, gave a tuning fork to Handel: it sounds a C at 512 Hz.
Vers 1280, Franco de Cologne fixe les ra: Around 1280, Franco of Cologne set out the ratios between note values. Values then slowed down over the centuries: the semibreve, once a short note, became our whole note, the longest in routine use.
En 1322, l'Ars nova de Philippe de Vitry: In 1322, Philippe de Vitry's Ars nova introduced values shorter than the semibreve, including the minim, ancestor of our half note. Around the mid-15th century, scribes began drawing hollow notes.
Les clés sont à l'origine des lettres, F: Clefs began as letters, F, C and sometimes G, written at the start of a line in Gregorian chant. Their shape became stylised over time; the top flourish of the G clef probably comes from a cursive S, for "sol".
En Italie, « ut » devient « do » au XVII: In Italy, "ut" became "do" in the 17th century, and "si" was added later as the seventh syllable. In English-speaking countries, Sarah Glover changed it to "ti" in the 19th century.
Du XIVe au XVIe siècle, la musique s'écr: From the 14th to the 16th century, music was written without bar lines, using mensuration signs; our C and cut-C signs descend from them. In 1597, Thomas Morley was already mocking the confusion of these signs.
Vers 1750, les paysans de Bavière, du Ty: Around 1750, peasants in Bavaria, Tyrol and Styria danced the Walzer. It was long thought indecent because of the close embrace: a 1771 novel denounced "the shameless, indecent whirling-dance of the Germans". It reached Vienna around the 1780s.
On attribue à Guido d'Arezzo, vers l'an: The modern staff lines are attributed to Guido d'Arezzo, around the year 1000: his four-line staff is still used for Gregorian chant. The five-line staff appeared in Italy in the 13th century, but people still wrote on four, five or six lines around 1600.
Né à Fossombrone en 1466, Ottaviano Petr: Born in Fossombrone in 1466, Ottaviano Petrucci obtained from Venice in 1498 the exclusive right to print music for twenty years. Each sheet went through the press three times: the staves, then the notes, then the text. The Odhecaton gathers 96 chansons, including works by Josquin des Prez.
Les notes creuses, comme la blanche, app: Hollow notes, like the half note, appeared around the mid-15th century: in moving from parchment to paper, scribes avoided large ink dots, which paper handled poorly.
Les plus anciennes tablettes d'accord, e: The oldest tuning tablets, in cuneiform, describe a nine-stringed lyre with two strings set an octave from others; yet Sumerian and Akkadian have no known word for the octave.
L'accord par quintes est plus ancien que: Tuning by fifths is older than Pythagoras: it goes back to ancient Mesopotamia. In Europe, so-called "Pythagorean" tuning remained in use until the early 16th century, before meantone temperament.
Le bémol est à l'origine un b minuscule: The flat sign began as a stylised lowercase b: in Italian be molle, the "soft B".
Le monocorde, une seule corde tendue sur: The monochord, a single string stretched over a box with a movable bridge, was said to have been reinvented by Pythagoras in the 6th century BC; it served as a teaching tool throughout the Middle Ages. In 1618, Robert Fludd drew a "divine monochord" linking the universe to musical intervals.
En 1589, Vincenzo Galilei, le père de Ga: In 1589, Vincenzo Galilei, Galileo's father, showed that the story did not hold up. Mersenne explained why in 1636: a string's frequency follows the square root of the tension, so it takes four times the weight to go up an octave.
Le la à 440 Hz avait déjà été recommandé: A at 440 Hz had already been recommended in Stuttgart in 1834, based on Scheibler's work. In France, a law of 16 February 1859 set A at 435 Hz, after singers complained. In 1939, 440 was preferred to 439, a prime number hard to reproduce in a laboratory.
La plus ancienne œuvre notée presque com: The oldest nearly complete notated work, the Hymn to Nikkal, was inscribed around 1400 BC on a tablet from Ugarit, in Syria, found in the 1950s: its interval names already point to a diatonic, seven-note scale.
Le premier schéma du cycle des quintes f: The first diagram of the circle of fifths appears in Mykola Dyletsky's Grammatika, in 1677. Johann David Heinichen drew his own "musical circle" in 1711, independently.
Des civilisations très éloignées l'ont i: Distant civilisations each invented it on their own: Chinese music draws five modes from it, named gong, shang, jue, zhi and yu. Debussy and Ravel used it widely, and the blues scale derives from it.
Bach réunit le premier livre en 1722 à K: Bach compiled the first book in 1722 in Köthen, "for the profit and use of musical youth desirous of learning", and the second twenty years later in Leipzig. He knew Johann Caspar Ferdinand Fischer's Ariadne musica (1702). Both books were only printed in 1801.
Vers 1400 av. J.-C., l'Hymne à Nikkal d': Around 1400 BC, the Hymn to Nikkal from Ugarit, the oldest nearly complete notated music, is already based on a diatonic scale, played on a nine-stringed lyre.
Le cycle des quintes est d'abord dessiné: The circle of fifths was first drawn in 1677 by Mykola Dyletsky, then in 1711 by Johann David Heinichen. Attributing it to Pythagoras is an anachronism.
Joseph Sauveur resta muet jusqu'à 7 ans: Joseph Sauveur remained mute until age 7 because of a hearing and speech impairment. Yet he is credited with coining the word "acoustique"; he presented his research on sound to the Academy of Sciences in 1701.
Helmholtz parlait de Klangfarbe, la « co: Helmholtz spoke of Klangfarbe, "tone colour". Debussy gave timbre an unprecedented structural role in music.
Euler, d'Alembert et Daniel Bernoulli av: Euler, d'Alembert and Daniel Bernoulli had studied such series in connection with vibrating strings. Fourier announced his discovery in 1807, in a memoir on the propagation of heat; a committee including Lagrange later criticised its lack of rigour.
Helmholtz décrit ses résonateurs en 1863: Helmholtz described his resonators in 1863 in On the Sensations of Tone. Rudolph Koenig later built a sound analyser from them.
Vers 1700, le facteur allemand Johann Ch: Around 1700, German maker Johann Christoph Denner invented the clarinet by adding a register key to the chalumeau. Because its cylindrical bore favours odd harmonics, it overblows at the twelfth, not the octave.
Sauveur, qui a nommé les nœuds des corde: Sauveur, who named the nodes of vibrating strings, had been mute until age 7. He is also credited with the word "acoustique".
Gioseffo Zarlino est le premier, au XVIe: Gioseffo Zarlino was the first, in the 16th century, to make the three-note chord the foundation of music. Johannes Lippius coined the phrase "harmonic triad" in 1612.
Rameau, qui pose la théorie des renverse: Rameau, who set out the theory of inversions, fell out with Jean-Jacques Rousseau from 1745; the Querelle des Bouffons (1752-1754) then accused him of writing outdated, overly complicated music.
Le mot vient du latin cadentia, « chute: The word comes from the Latin cadentia, "a falling". Guido d'Arezzo first discussed it in his Micrologus: two voices meeting in unison at the end of a phrase.
Rameau, alors presque quadragénaire, pub: Rameau, then nearly forty, published his treatise on settling back in Paris, and became famous as a theorist. His first opera, Hippolyte et Aricie, only came in 1733, when he was about 50.
Gioseffo Zarlino devient maître de chape: Gioseffo Zarlino became maestro di cappella of St Mark's in Venice in 1565. Among his students was Vincenzo Galilei, Galileo's father.
Euclide est le premier à donner la propo: Euclid was the first to give this comma's ratio, 531,441:524,288. Chinese mathematicians also knew it as early as 122 BC: the calculation appears in the Huainanzi.
Le cent apparaît d'abord en 1875, dans l: The cent first appeared in 1875, in Alexander Ellis's translation of Helmholtz's book, and was defined in 1880. As early as 1832, Gaspard de Prony had proposed a logarithmic unit, but equal to a whole semitone.
En 1584, dans le Fronimo, Vincenzo Galil: In 1584, in Fronimo, Vincenzo Galilei set lute frets with an approximate ratio of 18:17. Around 1605, Simon Stevin was the first in the West to link equal temperament to the twelfth root of 2, in a manuscript only published in 1884.
En 1584, Zhu Zaiyu publie une méthode tr: In 1584, Zhu Zaiyu published a very precise method: he divided string lengths successively by the twelfth root of 2. In 1630, Johann Faulhaber published a monochord table, still full of errors.
Vers 50 av. J.-C., le Chinois Jing Fang: Around 50 BC, China's Jing Fang continued the fifths up to the 53rd: the remaining gap is much smaller than the Pythagorean comma. It was later named Mercator's comma.
Zhu Zaiyu était un prince Ming : il héri: Zhu Zaiyu was a Ming prince: he inherited the title Prince of Zheng in 1593 and quickly gave it up to his cousin. He also accurately calculated the length of the tropical year to correct the calendar.
Alexander Ellis définit le cent en 1880: Alexander Ellis defined the cent in 1880 as "1200 equal hundredths of an equal semitone" across the octave. He officially introduced it in 1885 to compare the scales of different nations.
Le mot « bien tempéré » figure dès 1681: The phrase "well tempered" already appears in 1681 in the subtitle of Andreas Werckmeister's Orgelprobe, who proposed tunings with eight pure fifths. Bach's exact tuning is the subject of several reconstructions.
Au début du XIXe siècle, les accordeurs: In the early 19th century, tuners reached almost modern precision. In the second half of the century, tuning by counting beats spread, popularised by Helmholtz and Ellis.
Les ingénieurs du téléphone mesuraient d: Telephone engineers first measured losses in "miles of standard cable". In 1924, Bell Labs created the "transmission unit", renamed the decibel in 1928.
Fletcher and Munson measured with headphones. In 1956, Robinson and Dadson redid the measurements with loudspeakers; a new standard, ISO 226, replaced them in 2003, combining data from several countries.
Le gouverneur de Géorgie Zell Miller pro: Georgia governor Zell Miller nonetheless proposed in 1998 to give every newborn a classical music CD. In 2010, a meta-analysis by Pietschnig still found no notable effect.
Le bel, dix fois plus grand, porte le no: The bel, ten times larger, is named after Alexander Graham Bell; it is rarely used, since in practice people work in decibels.
La symphonie est une commande de la Soci: The symphony was commissioned by the Philharmonic Society of London in 1817. On 7 May 1824, at the Theater am Kärntnertor, Michael Umlauf conducted; Beethoven, standing on stage, gave the tempos while turning the pages of his score. The audience gave him five standing ovations.
L'oreille absolue est étudiée scientifiq: Absolute pitch was studied scientifically from the 19th century. It is often said to occur in one person in 10,000, a figure that may be wrong; according to Diana Deutsch and colleagues (2006), it is far more common among those who grew up in East Asia, with a tonal language.
